UPSTREAM: soc/intel/common/block: Common ACPI This patch adds the common acpi code.ACPI code is very similar accross different intel chipsets.This patch is an effort to move those code in common place so that it can be shared accross different intel platforms instead of duplicating for each platform. We are removing the common acpi files in src/soc/intel/common. This removes the acpi.c file which was previously in src/soc/common/acpi. The config for common acpi is SOC_INTEL_COMMON_BLOCK_ACPI which can be defined in SOC's Kconfig file in order to use the common ACPI code. This patch also includes the changes in APL platform to use the common ACPI block. TEST= Tested the patch as below: 1.Builds and system boots up with the patch. 2.Check all the ACPI tables are present in /sys/firmware/acpi/tables 3.Check SCI's are properly working as we are modifying the function to override madt. 4.Extract acpi tables like DSDT,APIC, FACP, FACS and decompile the by iasl and compare with good known tables. 5.Execute the extracted tables in aciexec to check acpi methods are working properly. Change-Id: I68f93d48fd1225351bcbbb5ad089b43c78c2be1d Signed-off-by: Patrick Georgi <pgeorgi@google.com> Original-Commit-Id: bd427803ab18576462c2c179c94ec0fec819221c Original-Change-Id: Ib6eb6fd5366e6e28fd81bc22d050b0efa05a2e5d Original-Signed-off-by: Shaunak Saha <shaunak.saha@intel.com> Original-Reviewed-on: https://review.coreboot.org/20630 Original-Tested-by: build bot (Jenkins) <no-reply@coreboot.org> Original-Reviewed-by: Aaron Durbin <adurbin@chromium.org> Original-Reviewed-by: Sumeet R Pawnikar <sumeet.r.pawnikar@intel.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/659540 Commit-Ready: Patrick Georgi <pgeorgi@chromium.org> Tested-by: Patrick Georgi <pgeorgi@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Patrick Georgi <pgeorgi@chromium.org>

UPSTREAM: drivers/intel/fsp1_1: Adjust check for FSP header revision With FSP 1.1, all FSP blobs are forward-compatible with newer FSP 1.1 header files, so adjust the header revision check to ensure that the FSP blob isn't newer than the header, rather than an exact version match. This resolves a version mismatch issue with Braswell ChromeOS devices, which ship with FSP blobs newer than the publicly-released blob (1.1.2.0), but older than the current Braswell FSP 1.1 header (1.1.7.0). TEST: build/boot google/cyan and edgar boards, observe no adverse effects from using current FSP header (1.1.7.0) with the factory- shipped FSP blobs (1.1.4.0/1.1.4.2). BUG=none BRANCH=none TEST=none Change-Id: I1a47aa633ec9bd8781faf8b84c465d4a0d5a89c6 Signed-off-by: Patrick Georgi <pgeorgi@google.com> Original-Commit-Id: 77c01e1f2f16bc24a45e68b0c413e510dc19a756 Original-Change-Id: I8934675a2deed260886a83fa34512904c40af8e1 Original-Signed-off-by: Matt DeVillier <matt.devillier@gmail.com> Original-Reviewed-on: https://review.coreboot.org/21369 Original-Reviewed-by: Aaron Durbin <adurbin@chromium.org> Original-Tested-by: build bot (Jenkins) <no-reply@coreboot.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/659541 Commit-Ready: Patrick Georgi <pgeorgi@chromium.org> Tested-by: Patrick Georgi <pgeorgi@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Patrick Georgi <pgeorgi@chromium.org>

UPSTREAM: cpu/x86/mp_init: remove adjust_cpu_apic_entry() The original purpose of adjust_cpu_apic_entry() was to set up an APIC map. That map was effectively only used for mapping *default* APIC id to CPU number in the SMM handler. The normal AP startup path didn't need this mapping because it was whoever won the race got the next cpu number. Instead of statically calculating (and wrong) just initialize the default APIC id map when the APs come online. Once the APs are online the SMM handler is loaded and the mapping is utilized. flashrom: Find programs in default PATH instead of using `which`. The utility 'which' is not a shell built-in command, and what it does is simpy trying to find programs in default PATH. This implies calling `which` then use the output for complete path sent to execv is identical to directly calling execvp (which uses PATH). In issue chromium:763264, we think in special environment like initramfs, calling 'which' may not work properly even if PATH is set. This change tries to replace execv by execvp, and simply use 'flashrom' if the system is not Android; which reduced dependency and complexity of calling flashrom.
